proposal.explanation: The discovery trace shows rst asserted at cycle 8, then drop_frame incorrectly high at cycles 13-14, followed by output_axis_tdata/tlast/tvalid mismatches at cycle 16. The highest-leverage fixes are completing the reset block (patch_06b184d83718 covers both drop_frame and wr_ptr_cur; patch_15a85deae41e and patch_9d300784e043 each cover one), then guarding the drop-frame entry condition against reset (patch_a0bad4f15d79) and against spurious writes (patch_cc5c635bb718, patch_5d8c1cfb86b1, patch_e68873b48903). The ready gating (patch_c8cdd17adad4) is included as a secondary handshake fix. All cited patches reference line numbers in the original source and tie to the first failing port drop_frame at cycles 13-14.

ranking.mechanism: Reset block missing explicit initialization of drop_frame and wr_ptr_cur; discovery trace shows rst asserted at cycle 8 and drop_frame=1 at cycles 13-14. Adding both resets clears the partial-frame drop state and current write pointer together, directly addressing the first observed mismatches on drop_frame.

Reset block initializes wr_ptr but not wr_ptr_cur; trace shows rst at cycle 8. Resetting wr_ptr_cur prevents stale current-write pointer from corrupting the first post-reset frame, which is consistent with the early drop_frame mismatches.

Reset block does not clear drop_frame; discovery shows rst at cycle 8 and drop_frame=1 at cycles 13-14. Adding drop_frame<=0 on reset directly clears the drop-state register that is observed high when it should be low.

Drop-frame entry condition (full|full_cur|drop_frame) unguarded during reset; rst=1 at cycle 8. Qualifying with !rst prevents the drop logic from triggering on the reset cycle, which matches the first drop_frame mismatch at cycle 13 after reset release.

input_axis_tready driven by (~full|DROP_WHEN_FULL) without rst gating; rst=1 at cycle 8. Adding &&(!rst) suppresses ready during reset so the upstream source cannot push data into a resetting FIFO, indirectly reducing spurious drop_frame activation.

Write-block guard 'write' lacks !drop_frame qualifier; trace shows drop_frame=1 at cycles 13-14. Changing to (write)&&(!drop_frame) stops new writes from entering the drop-frame handling path once drop_frame is set, limiting the window where drop_frame can be asserted.

Drop-frame condition (full|full_cur|drop_frame) missing write qualification; cycles 13-14 show drop_frame=1. Adding &&(write) ensures the drop logic only evaluates on actual write cycles, aligning the condition with the write enable that drives pointer updates.

Same condition as above but qualified with write instead of !write; both target the drop-frame entry guard at line 100 where the first mismatches appear, ensuring drop_frame logic only runs when a write occurs.
